reason: The text depicts Joseph's elevation to power and leadership in Egypt based entirely on wisdom, foresight, and administrative competence. Joseph is chosen as leader (וַיֹּ֤אמֶר פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֔ף אַחֲרֵ֨י הוֹדִ֧יעַ אֱלֹהִ֛ים אוֹתְךָ֖ אֶת־ כָּל־ זֹ֑את אֵין־ נָב֥וֹן וְחָכָ֖ם כָּמֽוֹךָ) specifically because he is 'wise and discerning,' not because of any capacity for violence. His leadership is demonstrated through dream interpretation, famine preparation, grain storage, and resource distribution. When famine arrives, people come to Joseph for bread—there is no mention of violence, coercion, or force against disobedient subjects. The passage presents an explicit counterthesis to the proposed statement: good leadership emerges from wisdom and prudent planning.
